about: Of all the offertory prayers only this one says what the sacrifice is a memorial of, and it names three things: the passion, the resurrection and the ascension. It is also the only one addressed to the Trinity — the others speak to the Father, or to God without qualification. The word “istórum” points to what is close at hand: the saints whose relics are in the altar, the same ones the priest named at the beginning of Mass as he kissed it. The last sentence falls into two halves: they intercede for us in heaven, we keep their memory on earth — in cælis and in terris stand at the two ends of one clause.

s01.narrative: The priest returns to the middle of the altar, bows, and with joined hands resting on it offers the whole sacrifice together.

s02.translation: Receive, holy Trinity, this offering, which we offer thee in memory of the passion, the resurrection and the ascension of Jesus Christ our Lord: and in honour of blessed Mary ever Virgin, and of blessed John the Baptist, and of the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and of these, and of all the Saints: that it may profit them unto honour and us unto salvation: and may they deign to intercede for us in heaven, whose memory we keep on earth. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

w001.function: The same word that began the prayer over the host; the offertory closes with what opened it.

w003.function: The vocative is the same as the nominative; the address settles it.

w005.function: The noun of offérre — the thing carried up before God.

w010.function: Ob with the accusative means “on account of”; the same memory returns at the prayer's end as “memóriam” (w059).

w014.function: Three genitives depending on “memóriam” (w010) — the one place in the offertory that says what the sacrifice recalls.

w021.function: The change of preposition marks a change of ground: memory of Christ, honour of the saints.

w035.function: The same list of saints as in the Confíteor, here in the genitive.

w037.function: The demonstrative of what is close at hand: the saints whose relics are in this altar.

w042.function: Dative of advantage: it is to be of honour to them.

w049.function: Two sides of one offering: honour to them, salvation to us.

w051.function: Nominative plural, the subject of “dignéntur” (w055); the same spelling also serves the dative singular.

w054.function: Inter-cédere: to step between — to stand between the one asking and the one asked.

w062.function: “in cælis” and “in terris” stand at the two ends of one clause: they there, we here.

w064.function: Idem is is with the ending -dem, “the same one”; before d the m turns to n — hence eúndem, not eúmdem.
